transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's a dizziness I've been getting when I stand up — from a chair, or getting out of bed. It feels swimmy, like I'm about to faint, and it's been going on for about ten days now.
When did you first notice it?
It started about ten days ago. Looking back, it was roughly a week after I began a new blood-pressure tablet.
Is there anything that makes it better or worse?
It's worse first thing in the morning and if I stand up quickly. It settles if I sit back down for a minute or so.
How would you describe the feeling in your own words?
It's a swimmy sort of feeling, like I'm about to faint — not the room spinning round, if that makes sense.
Where exactly do you feel it, and does it spread anywhere?
I don't feel it in any one spot really — it's more a general light-headed feeling all over. I haven't noticed it spreading anywhere.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 10 is the worst, how bad is it?
I'd say about a 6 out of 10. It nearly made me fall once — I had to grab the kitchen worktop — but I haven't actually fallen.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It comes and goes — each episode only lasts less than a minute, but it happens several times a day.
Has anything else been bothering you along with this?
No, nothing else like that. I haven't had any chest pain, palpitations, blackouts, or weakness in my arms or legs.
Do you see a doctor regularly for any health condition?
Yes, I've had high blood pressure for about fifteen years. I also have osteoarthritis in both my hips.
Which medicines do you take regularly, including any new ones?

I started a new one about two and a half weeks ago — amlodipine 5 mg once a day, the practice nurse added it for my high readings. I also take bendroflumethiazide 2.5 mg, a water tablet, every morning, and I've been on that for years. Then there's a small tablet for my stomach each morning — I can't remember its name — and paracetamol 1 g up to three times a day for my hip pain.
Are you allergic to any medicines?
No, I'm not allergic to anything as far as I know.
Has this changed what you can do around the house or outside?
Well, I've stopped going to my Tuesday lunch club — I'm worried about feeling faint on the bus. Otherwise I've just been careful getting up.
Is there anything about this that worries you?
Yes — I'm worried the new blood-pressure tablet is causing this, and I'd like to know whether I should stop taking it.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
